newsitem.title: USA: Gore responds to muni concerns on Internet bill.
newsitem.headline: Gore responds to muni concerns on Internet bill.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore said Friday the Clinton Administration has not made a final decision on whether to endorse controversial Internet taxation legislation pending in the U.S. Congress, a Council of State Governments official said.
Daniel Sprague, the group's executive director, made the statement after a White House meeting between Gore and seven state and local government groups on Internet policy and other key issues.
Rep. Christopher Cox, R-Calif., and Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., introduced identical bills in March that would impose an indefinite moratorium on state and local taxation of commerce over the Internet.
The legislation would not affect existing taxes on goods and services ordered through the Internet, as long as the taxes were the same as those on mail order goods.
At a congressional hearing last month, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said the administration strongly supports the "goals and underlying objectives" of the legislation.
At Friday's hour-long meeting, Gore was told by the seven groups that they have "a real problem" with the administration's position on the bill, Sprague said.
States and localities oppose Internet legislation on the grounds that it could affect revenues.

Gore responded that Sommers was talking only in a "very general sense" and that the administration has not "weighed in on that issue yet. Our position has not been communicated in a final fashion," Gore said, according to Sprague.
